author: jakeconstantine
quote:
Thirteen years. Billions of dollars. Thousands of developers working crunch hours. And this is what we waited for? Grand Theft Auto VI isn’t a video game—it’s a painfully slow, hyper-realistic chore simulator wrapped around the exact same archaic, brain-dead mission design Rockstar has been recycling since the PlayStation 3 era.

If you have the attention span **** and get hypnotized by pretty puddle reflections and realistic sweat physics, you’ll love it. For anyone who actually cares about gameplay, it’s an insulting, bloated slog.

Rockstar’s Formula Has Officially Rotted
The disconnect between the open world and the actual missions is borderline satirical at this point. The game drops you into this massive, living state of Leonida, and then the second you start a mission, it puts a digital shock collar on your neck. Drive down this exact street. Park on this exact yellow dot. Shoot these guys from this exact chest-high wall. Breathe wrong or try to use an ounce of actual brainpower to flank an objective, and you get hit with a patronizing "MISSION FAILED" screen. It’s less like playing a sandbox game and more like being an unpaid extra on a movie set with a tyrannical director screaming at you every time you step off your mark.

Controls That Feel Like Wading Through Wet Cement
Whoever decided that "realism" means making your character handle like a drunk refrigerator needs to be fired. Turning around takes three business days. Picking up a single item requires watching a four-second animation of Lucia or Jason reaching out, grabbing it, examining it, and putting it in their pocket. Gunplay is still an absolute joke—without aggressive auto-aim snapping your reticle onto enemies' chests for you, the shooting feels like trying to aim a firehose in zero gravity. It isn't "immersive"; it's tedious, clunky, and actively hostile to the player's time.

Sanitized Satire Written by Corporate Cowards
Remember when GTA actually had teeth? GTA 6’s attempts at paroding modern social media and Florida culture feel like they were written by a 50-year-old marketing executive scrolling through TikTok trends from three years ago. Every joke is safe, toothless, and terrified of actually offending anyone. The story itself is a pacing nightmare—twenty hours of boring, repetitive "drive here, listen to exposition, shoot 40 brainless cops, drive back" filler sandwiched around a handful of decent cutscenes.

A Glorified Storefront Disguised as a Sequel
Worst of all, you can feel the greedy corporate fingerprints all over the single-player campaign. Whole storylines end abruptly with zero payoff because they were blatantly carved out to be recycled into GTA Online DLC. And speaking of Online—it’s a predatory, pay-to-win casino from day one. Want a basic sports car or a decent safehouse? Either treat this game like a full-time, unpaid second job, or pull out your credit card and buy Shark Cards on top of the absurd base price you already paid.

GTA 6 is the ultimate triumph of style over substance. It’s a gorgeous, lifeless tech demo that mistakes tedium for depth and graphics for innovation. Save your money, watch the cutscenes on YouTube, and let this dinosaur of a franchise finally go extinct.
